status.summary: Former UFC middleweight champion. He won the belt from Dricus Du Plessis (UD 50-44 x3, UFC 319, Aug 16, 2025) and lost it to Sean Strickland by split decision at UFC 328 (May 9, 2026), his first MMA loss. Pro record 15-1, UFC 9-1 (ESPN, Wikipedia, MMA Junkie). Ranked #1 at middleweight on both UFC lists and #11 (tied) pound-for-pound. No MMA fight is booked: he pushed for an immediate Strickland rematch, which the UFC passed over for Nassourdine Imavov, and on Oct 27, 2026 said he would follow Strickland to any division. Meanwhile he wrestles in Real American Freestyle (RAF; freestyle wrestling, not MMA): 4-0 there, most recently an 11-0 technical fall over Robbie Lawler at RAF 14 (Oct 23, 2026). He is booked to wrestle Colby Covington for the RAF cruiserweight crossover title in the RAF Abu Dhabi main event on Nov 14, 2026. Health: in September 2026 he said he has 'a lot of injuries', mainly his hands, and would take a one-to-two-month break to treat them if no UFC fight came by December.
status.ranking: #1 middleweight (UFC media panel, Nov 3-5, 2026; also #1 in the Meta UFC Rankings of Oct 31, 2026); #11 men's pound-for-pound, tied with Ciryl Gane (media panel, Nov 3-5, 2026). Read from ufcrankings.org and ufcalendar.com mirrors because ufc.com returned 403.
status.next_fight: No MMA bout booked. Scheduled freestyle-wrestling match (not MMA): vs Colby Covington for the RAF cruiserweight crossover title, RAF Abu Dhabi main event, Nov 14, 2026.

injuries.what: Hand problems he says need fixing ('It's just my hands. I punch hard so I always have problems with my hands'); said any break would be one or two months.
Said 'I have a lot of injuries' and that he goes into every fight with some problem; planned a break to treat them if not booked by December 2026.

signature: takedown chains from the first exchange: 12 of 17 vs Du Plessis (UFC 319), 9 of 13 vs Strickland (UFC 328), with 4:47 of R1 control in both (1 of 1 in R1 vs Du Plessis, 2 of 2 vs Strickland)
long top control: 21:40 of 25 minutes vs Du Plessis; 54% control share decayed
chokes: D'Arce (John Phillips 2020, Kevin Holland 2022) and rear-naked choke (Li Jingliang 2021, Robert Whittaker R1 3:34, Oct 2024)
ground strikes: TKO of Rhys McKee from mount (2020); 19 of 22 ground strikes in R3 vs Du Plessis
one-punch power standing: KO of Gerald Meerschaert at 0:17 of R1 (2020)
body punching on the feet when the takedowns stop: 35 of 65 body strikes landed vs Strickland
weaknesses: control drops after R1 and the opponent out-lands him on the feet in three of his four UFC decisions: Burns 101-81 over R2-R3 (2022; Chimaev's control fell from 1:44 to 0:10 and 0:29), Usman 33-22 over R2-R3 (2023), and Strickland 123-98 over R2-R5 (2026)
lost the title to a boxer who kept getting back up: after 4:47 of R1 control, he managed 0:04, 0:00 and 0:54 in R2-R4 vs Strickland, and his 6 takedowns in R5 bought only 1:31
his striking defense is only average when he is kept standing: Burns landed 119 sig strikes on him in 15 minutes
style.summary: A heavy, forceful wrestler who chains takedowns from the opening exchange, holds top position and finishes with chokes or ground strikes. When the first takedown sticks he can control a whole fight, as he did against Du Plessis. His three closest decisions all turned the same way: the opponent survived R1 and out-landed him on the feet after that.

moves.notes: Group shares follow fighters.json decayed sums: sig attempts 73.5% head, 20.5% body, 5.9% leg (career 80.5/14.2/5.2). The middleweight league is 77.2/14.0/8.8, so he goes to the body more than average and to the legs less. Much of his output is on the ground (24.8% of landed sig decayed, 40.9% career), and those strikes are drawn by the ground-strike tables, not these weights. On the feet, the cross leads the head group because his only distance KO is a single punch (Meerschaert) and no source in this pass describes a jab-led game. The body weights lean to hooks because the body volume vs Strickland (35 of 65) came in the open with no clinch time logged, which suggests punches more than kicks, though ufcstats does not say which. Leg strikes are rare; the inside kick gets the larger share as a judgment. Spinning is 0 because nothing in the data or prior coverage shows it. Knee and elbow are small judgments. Web scouting sources could not be opened in this pass, so the in-group weights are data-led judgments.

engine_notes.note: R1 is a wrestling round: in UFC 319 and UFC 328 he spent 4:47 of R1 on top both times and landed 1 and 0 sig strikes in those rounds. The ufcstats pace curve therefore reads 5.5x to 19x R1 in later rounds; that ratio reflects his near-zero R1 striking, not a late surge.

Control per round vs Du Plessis was 4:47, 4:47, 4:46, 4:26, 2:54. Vs Strickland it was 4:47, 0:04, 0:00, 0:54, 1:31, with Strickland logging 3:01 of control himself in R2. A takedown-success knob that decays after R1 would fit both fights.
Takedowns 5.8 per 15 min decayed at 62% (middleweight league 1.36 at 36%). Opponents rarely shoot on him (0.87 per 15 min).
Never knocked down in 10 UFC fights; no stoppage losses.
